source_evidence: Exact player 'What do you offer them?' asks Caul what her dependent subjects receive in exchange for imposed obligations. She claims security against marauders/creatures, road maintenance, market access, ability to distribute provisions in bad harvests, and accepts coin/labor/produce as contributions. These are her own claims about services, not an independently audited delivery history or new asset/expense. Cirren asks about blood tribute; she says blood contributors receive same protection, treats it as levy. When asked whether they may refuse, she acknowledges those already bound may not simply renounce obligations or depart without her consent, regards refusal as grounds for enforcement and argues durable protection requires enforceable allegiance. This is candid bounded disclosure of fixed coercive policy, not new individual atrocity, newly invented prisoner or verified exact rates. Cirren rejects treating a person's body as a tax obligation; Mara and Fenar observe. Caul's prior conditional offer of relinquishing customs tower in return for recognition of manor stewardship and subjects' obligations remains unaccepted. No player assent, negotiated reform, release, ownership, oath, roll, movement, combat, cost, rest or resource change. D334~19:58, V chooses reply.
